questions.knowledge_point: Finding a Block Diagonalization of a 3x3 Matrix
questions.problem:
$$
A=[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & -1 \\ -2 & 3 & 6 \\ 1 & 0 & 1\end{aligned}]
$$

Consider the matrix $A$ shown above. Find a block diagonal matrix $B,$ where the $2\times 2$ block represents a rotation-scaling matrix, such that $A=PB{P}^{-1}.$
questions.worked_solution:
Recall that if $A$ is a real $3\times 3$ matrix that has one real eigenvalue ${\lambda }_{1}$ with corresponding eigenvector ${v}_{1},$ and two complex eigenvalues ${\lambda }_{2}={\overset{―}{\lambda }}_{3}$ with corresponding eigenvectors ${v}_{2}={\overset{―}{v}}_{3},$ then $A=PB{P}^{-1},$ where

$$
B=[\begin{aligned}{\lambda }_{1} & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & \text{Re}({\lambda }_{2}) & \text{Im}({\lambda }_{2}) \\ 0 & -\text{Im}({\lambda }_{2}) & \text{Re}({\lambda }_{2})\end{aligned}],\,\,P=[\begin{aligned}| & | & | \\ {v}_{1} & \text{Re}({v}_{2}) & \text{Im}({v}_{2}) \\ | & | & |\end{aligned}].
$$

Swapping the blocks on the main diagonal of $B$ will result in switching the corresponding columns in $P.$

To compute the eigenvalues of $A,$ we solve the characteristic equation, as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}det(A-\lambda I) & =0 \\ |\begin{aligned}1-\lambda  & 0 & -1 \\ -2 & 3-\lambda  & 6 \\ 1 & 0 & 1-\lambda \end{aligned}| & =0 \\ (3-\lambda )((1-\lambda )^{2}-1(-1)) & =0 \\ (3-\lambda )({\lambda }^{2}-2\lambda +2) & =0\end{aligned}
$$

So, the real eigenvalue is 
${\lambda }_{1}=3.$
Now, using the quadratic formula, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}{\lambda }_{2,3} & =\frac{2\pm \sqrt{(-2)^{2}-4\cdot 1\cdot 2}}{2} \\  & =\frac{2\pm \sqrt{-4}}{2} \\  & =1\pm \text{i}.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the block diagonal matrix is

$$
B=[\begin{aligned}3 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 1 & 1 \\ 0 & -1 & 1\end{aligned}].
$$

questions.knowledge_point: Calculating the Invertible Matrix in Block Diagonal Form of an NxN Matrix
questions.problem:
Consider the vectors ${v}_{1}$ and ${v}_{3}$ and the block diagonal matrix $B$ shown below, where both $2\times 2$ blocks of $B$ represent rotation-scaling matrices:

$$
{v}_{1}=[\begin{aligned}1-\text{i} \\ 2+\text{i} \\ 5\text{i} \\ 2-\text{i}\end{aligned}],\,{v}_{3}=[\begin{aligned}3+2\text{i} \\ 1-\text{i} \\ 3-\text{i} \\ -5+2\text{i}\end{aligned}],\,B=[\begin{aligned}2 & -1 & 0 & 0 \\ 1 & 2 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 5 & 1 \\ 0 & 0 & -1 & 5\end{aligned}]
$$

The vectors ${v}_{1}$ and ${v}_{3}$ are the eigenvectors of a matrix $A$ corresponding to the eigenvalues ${\lambda }_{1}=2-\text{i}$ and ${\lambda }_{3}=\text{i}+5,$ respectively. 
Given that $A=PB{P}^{-1},$ which of the following could be the matrix $P?$
questions.worked_solution:
Recall that if $A$ is a $4\times 4$ real matrix that has complex eigenvalues 

$\,$ ${\lambda }_{1}={\overset{―}{\lambda }}_{2}\,$ and $\,{\lambda }_{3}={\overset{―}{\lambda }}_{4}$ 

with corresponding eigenvectors 

$\,$ ${v}_{1}={\overset{―}{v}}_{2}\,$ and $\,{v}_{3}={\overset{―}{v}}_{4},$ 

then $A=PB{P}^{-1},$ where

$$
B=[\begin{aligned}\text{Re}({\lambda }_{1}) & \text{Im}({\lambda }_{1}) & 0 & 0 \\ -\text{Im}({\lambda }_{1}) & \text{Re}({\lambda }_{1}) & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & \text{Re}({\lambda }_{3}) & \text{Im}({\lambda }_{3}) \\ 0 & 0 & -\text{Im}({\lambda }_{3}) & \text{Re}({\lambda }_{3})\end{aligned}]
$$

and

$$
P=[\begin{aligned}| & | & | & | \\ \text{Re}({v}_{1}) & \text{Im}({v}_{1}) & \text{Re}({v}_{3}) & \text{Im}({v}_{3}) \\ | & | & | & |\end{aligned}].
$$

Swapping the blocks on the main diagonal of $B$ will result in switching the corresponding columns in $P.$

From our block diagonal matrix

$$
B=[\begin{aligned}2 & -1 & 0 & 0 \\ 1 & 2 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 5 & 1 \\ 0 & 0 & -1 & 5\end{aligned}],
$$

we deduce that the first and second columns of $P$ correspond to the complex eigenvector ${v}_{1},$ and the third and forth columns of $P$ correspond to the complex eigenvector ${v}_{3}.$ Therefore,

$$
P=[\begin{aligned}1 & -1 & 3 & 2 \\ 2 & 1 & 1 & -1 \\ 0 & 5 & 3 & -1 \\ 2 & -1 & -5 & 2\end{aligned}].
$$

questions.problem:
Consider the vectors ${v}_{1}$ and ${v}_{3}$ and the block diagonal matrix $B$ shown below, where both $2\times 2$ blocks of $B$ represent rotation-scaling matrices:

$$
{v}_{1}=[\begin{aligned}-3+4\text{i} \\ 3+7\text{i} \\ 5 \\ 1\end{aligned}],\,{v}_{3}=[\begin{aligned}2 \\ 3+2\text{i} \\ 1+\text{i} \\ 3\end{aligned}],\,B=[\begin{aligned}-1 & 2 & 0 & 0 \\ -2 & -1 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 3 & -2 \\ 0 & 0 & 2 & 3\end{aligned}]
$$

The vectors ${v}_{1}$ and ${v}_{3}$ are the eigenvectors of a matrix $A$ corresponding to the eigenvalues ${\lambda }_{1}=-1+2\text{i}$ and ${\lambda }_{3}=3-2\text{i},$ respectively. 
Given that $A=PB{P}^{-1},$ which of the following could be the matrix $P?$
questions.worked_solution:
Recall that if $A$ is a $4\times 4$ real matrix that has complex eigenvalues 

$\,$ ${\lambda }_{1}={\overset{―}{\lambda }}_{2}\,$ and $\,{\lambda }_{3}={\overset{―}{\lambda }}_{4}$ 

with corresponding eigenvectors 

$\,$ ${v}_{1}={\overset{―}{v}}_{2}\,$ and $\,{v}_{3}={\overset{―}{v}}_{4},$ 

then $A=PB{P}^{-1},$ where

$$
B=[\begin{aligned}\text{Re}({\lambda }_{1}) & \text{Im}({\lambda }_{1}) & 0 & 0 \\ -\text{Im}({\lambda }_{1}) & \text{Re}({\lambda }_{1}) & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & \text{Re}({\lambda }_{3}) & \text{Im}({\lambda }_{3}) \\ 0 & 0 & -\text{Im}({\lambda }_{3}) & \text{Re}({\lambda }_{3})\end{aligned}]
$$

and

$$
P=[\begin{aligned}| & | & | & | \\ \text{Re}({v}_{1}) & \text{Im}({v}_{1}) & \text{Re}({v}_{3}) & \text{Im}({v}_{3}) \\ | & | & | & |\end{aligned}].
$$

Swapping the blocks on the main diagonal of $B$ will result in switching the corresponding columns in $P.$

From our block diagonal matrix

$$
B=[\begin{aligned}-1 & 2 & 0 & 0 \\ -2 & -1 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 3 & -2 \\ 0 & 0 & 2 & 3\end{aligned}],
$$

we deduce that the first and second columns of $P$ correspond to the complex eigenvector ${v}_{1},$ and the third and forth columns of $P$ correspond to the complex eigenvector ${v}_{3}.$ Therefore,

$$
P=[\begin{aligned}-3 & 4 & 2 & 0 \\ 3 & 7 & 3 & 2 \\ 5 & 0 & 1 & 1 \\ 1 & 0 & 3 & 0\end{aligned}].
$$

questions.knowledge_point: Calculating the Invertible Matrix in Block Diagonal Form of a 3x3 Matrix
questions.problem:
Consider the vectors ${v}_{1}$ and ${v}_{3}$ and the block diagonal matrix $B$ shown below, where the $2\times 2$ block of $B$ represents a rotation-scaling matrix:

$$
{v}_{1}=[\begin{aligned}3+5\text{i} \\ 1-6\text{i} \\ 4\text{i}\end{aligned}],\,{v}_{3}=[\begin{aligned}5 \\ 2 \\ 1\end{aligned}],\,B=[\begin{aligned}2 & 8 & 0 \\ -8 & 2 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & -5\end{aligned}]
$$

The vectors ${v}_{1}$ and ${v}_{3}$ are the eigenvectors of a matrix $A$ corresponding to the eigenvalues ${\lambda }_{1}=2+8\text{i}$ and ${\lambda }_{3}=-5,$ respectively. 
Given that $A=PB{P}^{-1},$ which of the following could be the matrix $P?$
questions.worked_solution:
Recall that if $A$ is a real $3\times 3$ matrix that has one real eigenvalue ${\lambda }_{3}$ with corresponding eigenvector ${v}_{3},$ and two complex eigenvalues ${\lambda }_{1}={\overset{―}{\lambda }}_{2}$ with corresponding eigenvectors ${v}_{1}={\overset{―}{v}}_{2},$ then $A=PB{P}^{-1},$ where

$$
B=[\begin{aligned}\text{Re}({\lambda }_{1}) & \text{Im}({\lambda }_{1}) & 0 \\ -\text{Im}({\lambda }_{1}) & \text{Re}({\lambda }_{1}) & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & {\lambda }_{3}\end{aligned}],\,\,P=[\begin{aligned}| & | & | \\ \text{Re}({v}_{1}) & \text{Im}({v}_{1}) & {v}_{3} \\ | & | & |\end{aligned}].
$$

Swapping the blocks on the main diagonal of $B$ will result in switching the corresponding columns in $P.$

From our block diagonal matrix

$$
B=[\begin{aligned}2 & 8 & 0 \\ -8 & 2 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & -5\end{aligned}],
$$

we deduce that the first and second columns of $P$ will correspond to the complex eigenvector ${v}_{1},$ and the third column of $P$ will correspond to the real eigenvector ${v}_{3}:$

$$
P=[\begin{aligned}3 & 5 & 5 \\ 1 & -6 & 2 \\ 0 & 4 & 1\end{aligned}]
$$

$$
